Report on education for children without Thai nationality and children of migrant workers approved; study visit to Chon Buri approved
se: The meeting considered the work of two subcommittees. First, the Subcommittee on Learning Promotion, Private Education, Special Education and Educational Equality presented its draft study report on education for children without Thai nationality and children of migrant workers (Myanmar), a case study of the work of private organisations in Samut Sakhon and Tak. The report finds that the main obstacles come from system-level problems and conditions in a ministerial regulation, so that as many as 96.7 per cent of these children leave the school system when they reach secondary level. It lists 7 structural problems, such as personal status and documents, data systems that are not linked, language, moving with their parents' work, and shortages of teachers and budget. Its proposals come in 3 stages. In the short term, within 1 year: temporary recognition of existing learning centres, a joint working group of 5 agencies, and an amendment to the 2004 ministerial regulation with conditions such as a database of every pupil in the state system and at least 30 per cent of class time for the Thai language, civic duties and Thai culture. In the medium term, 1–3 years: extending the MECC Model to provinces with many migrant workers. In the long term, 3–5 years or more: including the approach in national plans and talks with Myanmar on recognising qualifications. The meeting approved the draft report and asked for it to be prepared for the Senate under Rules 98 and 99 of the Senate Rules of Procedure 2019, to be passed on to the Cabinet and related agencies. Second, the Subcommittee on Higher Education, Science, Research and Innovation reported the status of 3 study reports: putting medical, health, agricultural and food research to use, which is waiting for a place on the Senate agenda, and cooperative and work-integrated education (CWIE) and raising Thai universities in international rankings, which are being checked for format. It also reported 7 study topics for fiscal year 2027 and the invitation of agencies to give information on the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on higher education and on linking vocational courses to higher education. The meeting approved a study visit and seminar in Chon Buri on 25–26 January.

Expanding dual vocational education: information from the Labour Ministry and the EEC
se: The education and vocational education subcommittee reported progress on policy proposals to expand and raise dual vocational education, with information from the Ministry of Labour, such as the labour market situation and the “Thai Mee Ngan Tham” jobs database, and from the Eastern Economic Corridor Office (EEC) on cooperation between businesses and vocational colleges and manpower needs in the area.
it: Policy proposals to expand and raise dual vocational education (Ministry of Labour, EEC)

Proposals to raise Thai universities in international rankings
se: A working group of the higher education subcommittee presented its draft report on raising Thai universities in international rankings, such as a special law and fund to push selected high-potential fields linked to the country's target industries, learning from foreign institutions that turn research into real products with private investment, and changing academic promotion criteria to give more weight to research that is actually used. The education and vocational education subcommittee then reported on its work.
